title: Tool for Visualizing Safety Benchmark Coverage Gaps Using Embedding Projections
original_idea: Embed all prompts from AILuminate, HELM Safety, and TrustLLM using a sentence transformer. Project to 2D with UMAP. Visualize cluster density and identify sparse regions representing coverage gaps. Publish as an interactive HTML artifact.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful but indirect: a visualization tool aids understanding of benchmark coverage but does not directly improve safety. Impact depends on adoption by benchmark designers.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Sentence transformers and UMAP are well-documented, CPU-friendly tools. Building an interactive HTML visualization is within reach of CS students with web skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: an interactive HTML visualization artifact. Well-bounded pipeline (embed, project, visualize). Some scope creep risk in making it interactive.

novelty.reasoning: While embedding-based analysis (UMAP, sentence transformers) and safety benchmarks (AILuminate, HELM, TrustLLM) are individually well-established, no published work applies dimensionality reduction visualization specifically to map coverage gaps across safety benchmarks. Coverage-guided testing exists in software testing (MNCOVER for NLP), and 'The Scales of Justitia' surveys safety evaluation comprehensively, but neither produces an interactive visual tool identifying sparse regions in safety benchmark prompt space. The idea combines known techniques in a novel application.

AILuminate.details: Confirmed as MLCommons benchmark with 12 hazard categories. Primary data source for the proposed tool.

HELM Safety.details: Confirmed via Stanford CRFM. Holistic Evaluation of Language Models covers safety dimensions.

TrustLLM.details: Known benchmark for trustworthiness evaluation of LLMs. Relevant as a data source.
